title: SAPO: Improving the Scalability and Accuracy of Quantum Linear Solver for Portfolio Optimization
problem: Quantum linear solvers for portfolio optimization suffer from poor scalability or insufficient accuracy; existing quantum HHL-based methods cannot efficiently handle large-scale financial problems with acceptable precision.
motivation: Portfolio optimization is computationally expensive; quantum computing promises polynomial/exponential speedup, but current quantum algorithms trade off scalability versus accuracy.
method: SAPO extends the HHL algorithm by integrating mean-variance financial theory into the quantum circuit design via equivalent transformations to improve scalability, and applies a min-max eigenvalue model calibrated on historical market data to refine quantum circuit parameters for high accuracy.
key_novelty: First to jointly optimize quantum circuit design and parameter settings using financial domain knowledge and historical data characteristics.
contributions: Quantum circuit design incorporating mean-variance theory for improved scalability
Min-max eigenvalue model for parameter refinement using historical financial data
36.94% complexity reduction versus basic HHL algorithm
1.46× accuracy improvement over hybrid HHL approaches
limitations: Evaluation on synthetic market data; real-world performance on quantum hardware not discussed.
